items.headline: Josh Allen puts on a show — Bills christen their new stadium 41-31
items.body: Buffalo's brand-new Highmark Stadium got a proper housewarming on Thursday night. Josh Allen was electric — three touchdowns through the air and two more on the ground, five total — as the Bills outlasted the Lions 41-31 in a Week 2 shootout. Both teams came in 1-0; Buffalo looks like the early class of the AFC.
items.say: You catch Thursday night? Josh Allen scored five touchdowns himself in the Bills' first-ever game at their new stadium — beat the Lions 41-31 in a shootout. The guy plays like a video-game character.

items.headline: Clinch season's here — the Brewers are division champs again
items.body: The playoff picture is snapping into focus. Milwaukee wrapped up its fourth straight NL Central title this week and owns the best record in all of baseball — a mark they've held since mid-August, which is wild for the sport's small-market darlings. The Dodgers locked up the NL West too, and the AL races are heading down to the final week.
items.say: Baseball's clinch season is on — the Brewers just won their division again and have the best record in the whole sport. Not bad for the little-market team. Your club still alive in the playoff hunt?

items.headline: Record-breakers — the Lynx are locking down the No. 1 seed
items.body: Minnesota has been the story of the WNBA season. The Lynx are closing in on the No. 1 overall seed and chasing the league's single-season wins record, with only the upstart Golden State Valkyries able to catch them for the top spot. Playoffs tip off Sept. 27, and right now Minnesota looks like the team to beat.
items.say: The Minnesota Lynx are having a monster WNBA season — about to lock up the top seed and chasing the all-time single-season wins record. That new Golden State expansion team is the only one who can even catch them. Playoffs start soon.

links.text: CBS — Lynx grab No. 1 seed, tie wins record

items.headline: Miley goes full dance-floor — 'Bass Persuades' is out
items.body: Miley Cyrus — now going simply by MILEY — dropped her 10th album 'Bass Persuades' today, a glittery, '80s-synth dance-pop record with a cheeky thesis: the title track keeps chanting 'the kids don't wanna dance.' It's her first release under the solo mononym, with features from Model/Actriz and Andrew Wyatt, and she's playing two Hollywood Bowl shows next month.
items.say: New Miley album out today — it's a full-on dance-pop thing, and she goes by just 'MILEY' now. The single's basically her yelling that nobody parties anymore, which is pretty funny. What's been on your rotation?

items.headline: East-meets-West hip-hop history — 'The Godbody' finally drops
items.body: One for the heads: rap legends Rakim, Kurupt and Masta Killa teamed up for 'The Godbody,' a coast-uniting album reportedly born from a vision Tupac once had. The guest list is absurd — Snoop Dogg, Raekwon, Ghostface Killah, KRS-One, Kool G Rap — and there's even an interlude pairing Eminem and Jay-Z together for the first time in 25 years.
items.say: There's a wild hip-hop album out today — Rakim, Kurupt and Masta Killa on one record with what feels like every legend guesting, and supposedly Eminem and Jay-Z on a track together for the first time in 25 years. The whole thing was Tupac's idea originally. You into old-school rap?

items.headline: Tove Lo goes independent — 'Estrus' arrives
items.body: Swedish pop favorite Tove Lo released her sixth album 'Estrus' today, her first fully on her own label. It's raw and personal — she's called it 'primal, contradicting emotional chaos' — digging into family and her own struggles, all wrapped in the moody electro-pop she does better than just about anyone. Lead single 'I'm Your Girl Right?' was filmed in São Paulo with 70 dancers.
items.say: New Tove Lo album out today — she's the 'Habits (Stay High)' one from a while back. Moody, danceable pop, and she put this one out totally independent. Good windows-down driving music.

items.headline: Tom Hardy's back — 'MobLand' returns for Season 2
items.body: Guy Ritchie's slick London crime saga 'MobLand' is back on Paramount+ today, with Tom Hardy's fixer Harry Da Souza caught between warring crime families — Pierce Brosnan and Helen Mirren very much included. Ten new episodes roll out on Fridays through November. It was one of streaming's biggest hits this year, and it's already been renewed for a third season.
items.say: MobLand's back today — that Guy Ritchie gangster show with Tom Hardy, Pierce Brosnan and Helen Mirren. Slick, brutal, very bingeable. You watch the first season?

items.headline: Oscar season is officially revving up
items.body: The fall movie race is on. The Toronto Film Festival — Hollywood's biggest Oscar launchpad — wraps this weekend and hands out its all-important People's Choice award Sunday, while Venice just crowned 'Woman Unknown' with its top prize and gave George Clooney a lifetime-achievement honor. Translation: the prestige films are coming, and everyone's already arguing about them.
items.say: Movie awards season is basically kicking off — the Toronto festival wraps this weekend, and that's usually where the year's Oscar contenders reveal themselves. Fall's when the good, serious movies start rolling out. Seen anything great lately?
